title: Research OpenAI batch mode
description: IO-003: [research] Investigate OpenAI batch API for cost-effective bulk processing. Document findings and feasibility.
notes:
## Research Findings

### OpenAI Batch API Overview
- Endpoints: /v1/chat/completions + 6 others
- Pricing: 50% discount vs real-time API
- Completion window: fixed 24 hours (no faster SLA)
- Max 50,000 requests per batch, 200 MB file limit
- Input: JSONL with custom_id, method, url, body fields
- Output order does NOT match input (use custom_id to map)
- All requests must target same model

### Feasibility for Siftrank
PARTIALLY COMPATIBLE:
- Within-round batches ARE independent (parallelizable via batch API)
- Cross-round sequencing NOT compatible (round N+1 depends on N)
- Retry with feedback NOT possible (siftrank retries malformed JSON)
- 24h latency makes multi-round ranking take days

### Cost Savings
- 50% savings on all models
- Typical 100-doc run: ~$0.04 real-time vs ~$0.02 batch (gpt-4o-mini)
- Large 1000-doc run: ~$2.50-5.00 real-time vs ~$1.25-2.50 batch (gpt-4o)

### Recommendation
IMPLEMENT AS OPT-IN --batch FLAG (low priority):
- Opt-in for cost-sensitive bulk jobs, not replacing real-time
- Consider single-round mode first (skip convergence)
- Retry failures via follow-up batch
- Only valuable at scale; most users prefer real-time latency

Sources: https://developers.openai.com/api/docs/guides/batch/

title: Research file descriptor optimization for TOCTOU mitigation

title: Epic 5: Implement TOCTOU mitigation via file descriptor passing
